description: Excessive guard clauses add to cyclomatic complexity and make code harder to read. Centralize error handling in one place rather than scattering defensive checks throughout the code. Let code fail fast with clear errors rather than silently handling missing components. Only use guards for legitimate business logic where a barrier might not be there. Having something misconfigured or missing is not a legitimate business reason for a guard.

examples.description: Centralize error handling and let code fail fast
content: Assume components are properly initialized
Let exceptions propagate to centralized error handlers
Use type hints and contracts to document expectations
Fail fast with clear error messages
Correct Examples (no excessive guards):
- Direct access: self.knowledge.instructions (assumes knowledge exists)
- Direct property: self.behavior.bot_paths (assumes behavior exists)
- Direct method call: file.read_text() (let it fail if file missing)
Legitimate Business Logic Guards (keep these):
- if not user.is_authorized: return (business rule - user might not have permission)
- if item.is_sold: return (business rule - item state check)
- if not self._cache.is_valid(): refresh() (business logic - cache might be stale)
Centralized Error Handling:
- Handle errors at boundaries (API endpoints, CLI entry points)
- Use decorators or middleware for common error handling
- Let exceptions bubble up to appropriate handler
- Document expected state in docstrings/type hints

examples.description: Don't scatter defensive checks for misconfiguration throughout code
content: Don't check if every variable exists before using it
Don't use hasattr() checks everywhere
Don't check file.exists() before reading (let file operations fail if file missing)
Don't check isinstance() defensively
Don't check variable truthiness before every operation
Don't guard against missing configuration entries (let code fail fast)
Wrong Examples (excessive guards for misconfiguration):
- if self.knowledge and self.knowledge.instructions: (assume knowledge exists)
- if file.exists(): file.read() (let read fail if missing)
- if hasattr(obj, 'attr'): obj.attr (assume attr exists)
- if isinstance(obj, Type): obj.method() (trust type system)
- if not config_value: return None (let it fail if misconfigured)
- if not template_filename: return None (let it fail if misconfigured)
Excessive Guard Indicators (misconfiguration, not business logic):
- File existence checks before file operations
- hasattr() checks before attribute access
- Variable truthiness checks for required components
- None checks for required variables
- Guards checking optional configuration values
- Defensive checks that hide initialization problems
